To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) PPRV infection induces a strong T cell response in sheep; 2) vaccination with recombinant viruses induces T cell responses against epitopes that arise during PPRV challenge; 3) these T cell responses are important for the control of PPRV; and 4) vaccination with recomombinant viruses can be used for DIVA strategies.

we identified T cell epitopes from PPRV and showed that vaccination using recombinant Adenovirus expressing Peste des petits Ruminants Virus (PPRV) F and H proteins induced a strong T cell response to these epitopes and led to the generation of memory T cell responses.

The main takeaway from our work is that

recombinant vaccines based on adenovirus expressing either PPRV-F, -H, or both, can induce T cell responses to PPRV epitopes that arise during infection, and that these epitopes can be used for DIVA vaccination strategies.
